title: Civil Aviation (Unmanned Aircraft Levy) Bill 2020
portfolio: Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development and Communications

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: This bill is part of a package that would introduce a levy on certain drone and model aircraft operators to recover the cost of regulating them.
The bill would impose the levy for remotely piloted aircraft, with the amount set in regulations and capped at $300.
Collection would start on 30 September 2020, but the levy would not apply to model aircraft until 2022.
changes: The bill would establish the legal mechanism to impose a levy for cost recovery of regulatory services for remotely piloted aircraft operators.
It would define key terms such as 'RPA' and 'model aircraft' as in the Civil Aviation Safety Regulations.
It would cap the levy at $300 and allow it to be set to nil.
summary.affected: Commercial and professional users of remotely piloted aircraft and, from 2022, relevant model aircraft operators.

speeches.speaker: Michael McCormack
speeches.brief: Two bills were introduced to establish a cost-recovery levy on commercial remotely piloted aircraft (drone) operators to fund the Civil Aviation Safety Authority’s regulatory functions, with no levy set for the current financial year.

speeches.speaker: Michael McCormack
speeches.brief: The Civil Aviation Amendment (Unmanned Aircraft Levy Collection and Payment) Bill 2020 establishes a mechanism for the Commonwealth to pay the Civil Aviation Safety Authority (CASA) the levy amounts collected from remotely piloted aircraft operators, supporting long-term safe and lawful operations.

speeches.speaker: Catherine King
speeches.brief: The opposition supports the drone levy bills but will move an amendment, citing concerns that registration fees of up to $300 are far higher than comparable fees of $16 in the UK, $7 in the US and $5 in Canada. The speaker also criticised the government for failing to support the broader aviation sector during COVID-19, noting 3,000 job losses at Virgin, 5,000 at Dnata and 8,500 at Qantas, and called for a sector-wide aviation recovery plan.

speeches.speaker: Julian Simmonds
speeches.brief: The speaker supported the Civil Aviation (Unmanned Aircraft Levy) Bill 2020 and related bill to fund CASA's regulation of drones, with fees ranging from $0 to $300, to improve safety through training and registration, but also criticised CASA's bureaucratic over-regulation of recreational and general aviation, calling for reform to reduce costs and barriers.

speeches.speaker: Andrew Gee
speeches.brief: The bills enable CASA to continue regulating remotely piloted aircraft (drones) through a cost-recovery levy on commercial operators, with registration starting 30 September 2020 but no fees until mid-2021; recreational users are exempt.
